rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the first experiment should test the core multimodal hypothesis with a well-motivated strong configuration to establish a performance baseline and reduce uncertainty about whether combining modalities is beneficial. config_007 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) uses the most powerful available encoders (scGPT for RNA captures biological structure; ViT-L for images) and multiprofile to maximize information from each modality. Transformer aggregation provides flexible cross-profile integration, and concat fusion is a simple, robust baseline that avoids potential issues with learned weighting in an unexplored space. If this performs well, we gain a strong candidate to refine over the remaining 9 experiments (varying fusion, encoders, aggregation). If it underperforms, the result diagnoses whether the bottleneck is in multimodal fusion, a specific encoder, or the architecture, guiding targeted follow-up experiments. Starting with the most promising configuration is the best use of experiment 1 because it either immediately identifies a high-accuracy candidate or provides a clear anchor for decomposition in subsequent trials.

With only one completed experiment (config_007: multimodal/multiprofile/scgpt/ViT-L/transformer/concat at 50.7% acc), evidence is sparse and the most important uncertainty is whether the complex transformer aggregation over cells is actually contributing or introducing overfitting/noise. Config_009 changes exactly one variable—aggregation from transformer to avgpool—while keeping scgpt, ViT-L, multiprofile, and concat fusion identical to config_007. This clean A/B test will clarify whether the attention-based aggregation is a meaningful driver of the current performance or whether a simpler mean-pooling suffices. If avgpool matches or beats transformer, it frees us to focus budget on RNA/image encoder choices; if it is substantially worse, it confirms transformer aggregation as a key component. This is the highest-information single-variable probe available at experiment 2, reducing uncertainty about a high-impact architectural choice before committing remaining budget to other dimensions.

Evidence: config_009 (avgpool, concat) outperforms config_007 (transformer, concat) by ~1% acc and ~3% F1 with all other settings identical (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l), suggesting avgpool is the better aggregation. Uncertainty: we have not yet tested whether weighted fusion can further improve over concat fusion under the same avgpool aggregation. This experiment (config_003) tests that single variable change (concat → weighted) while holding the best-performing aggregation and all other settings constant. It is the best use of this slot because it is a minimal, controlled extension of the current best result, directly reducing uncertainty about the fusion strategy before we invest remaining budget in exploring other axes (RNA encoder, image encoder, modality ablations).

All three completed experiments share the same backbone (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile) and only vary aggregation/fusion, with avgpool+weighted (config_003, acc=0.542) clearly best. The major untested variable is the RNA encoder: we have only tried scgpt. Config_031 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) keeps all other settings at their best-known values while swapping in a simpler, high-dimensional PCA representation. This directly tests whether scgpt's learned representation is actually contributing or whether a standard linear projection suffices. If PCA matches or beats scgpt, it frees us to explore other dimensions; if it falls well short, it confirms scgpt is important and we should focus remaining budget on image encoder or profile setting. With 6 experiments left, resolving this core architectural question early maximizes the information gained per experiment.

The current best (config_031, acc=0.635) uses pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted. With scgpt, avgpool consistently outperformed transformer (0.518 vs 0.507), but pca_n2000 produces fundamentally different (linear, low-dim) representations that may interact differently with transformer aggregation. Config_012 is a clean single-variable test (avgpool→transformer, all else held at known-best) that clarifies whether the aggregation choice is robust or whether the PCA representation unlocks a benefit from attention-based aggregation. This is the highest-information next step: if transformer matches or beats avgpool, it opens a new direction; if it confirms avgpool, we can confidently lock that choice and spend remaining budget on the image encoder or fusion variable.

The best result so far is config_031 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) at 0.635 accuracy, and the evidence strongly supports pca_n2000 + avgpool + weighted as the optimal architecture. However, the image encoder dimension is unexplored for this strong combination—we've only tested imagenet_vit_l. Config_020 (pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) is a clean single-variable change that tests whether resnet50 could outperform or match imagenet_vit_l. This is the highest-value uncertainty to resolve: if resnet50 is comparable or better, it opens a new direction; if clearly worse, it confirms imagenet_vit_l is optimal and lets us focus remaining budget on other levers (e.g., profile setting or fusion). With 4 experiments left, efficiently confirming or ruling out the image encoder choice is critical before committing to fine-tuning.

The evidence strongly favors pca_n2000 + avgpool + weighted (config_020: 0.639, config_031: 0.635), and avgpool consistently outperforms transformer while weighted outperforms concat across all tested pairs. However, scvi_n2000 has never been tested in this proven-best architecture. Config_028 (scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) isolates the RNA encoder variable within the confirmed optimal aggregation/fusion/image-encoder setting. This is the highest-information experiment: if scvi_n2000 is competitive, it opens a new exploration axis for the remaining 3 experiments; if not, it confirms pca_n2000 is the optimal RNA encoder and we can focus remaining budget on fine-tuning around config_020. Testing transformer or concat variants would be low-value given their consistent underperformance, making this the best use of experiment 7.

The current best (config_028: scvi_n200 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted, acc=0.678) clearly establishes scvi_n200 as the superior RNA encoder and avgpool+weighted as the best aggregation/fusion pair. The key remaining uncertainty is the image encoder choice: resnet50 has only 2 data points (0.639, 0.678) vs. imagenet_vit_l with 5 (0.507–0.635). Config_036 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted + multiprofile) directly tests whether the larger ViT-L image encoder, when paired with the best RNA encoder and proven aggregation/fusion, can match or exceed resnet50. This is the highest-impact untested combination: if imagenet_vit_l performs comparably or better, it opens a new optimization axis; if it underperforms, it confirms resnet50 is optimal and the last 2 experiments can focus on fine-tuning around the resnet50+scvi_n200 core. This single test resolves the most important remaining design uncertainty before the budget ends.

The current best (config_036, scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted, 0.706) has strong evidence for its encoder choices, but the aggregation choice with this specific encoder pair remains untested. Prior evidence shows avgpool > transformer by ~5% with pca_n2000 (config_031 vs 012) and ~3.5% with scgpt (config_003 vs 007), but scvi_n200 produces learned latent representations that may interact differently with attention-based aggregation. Config_038 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) directly tests whether transformer aggregation can match or exceed avgpool with the strongest encoder combination. If it underperforms as expected, it confirms the current best architecture is near-optimal, giving confidence to accept 0.706 in the final experiment. If it surprisingly performs well, it could push past 0.706. This is the highest-information experiment among the remaining options, as it resolves the last major architectural uncertainty in the neighborhood of the best configuration with only 1 experiment left in the budget.

The current best (config_038: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725) establishes that scvi_n200, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion are the strongest components. The key remaining uncertainty is whether the transformer aggregation benefit is specific to imagenet_vit_l or generalizable across image encoders. config_045 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer + weighted) isolates this interaction: we know scvi_n200+resnet50+avgpool+weighted=0.678 (config_028), and transformer gave +0.019 over avgpool with imagenet_vit_l (0.706→0.725). If transformer aggregation also helps resnet50 comparably, this could reach ~0.697–0.71; if the interaction is synergistic, it could approach or exceed 0.725. Among all untested configs, this is the closest logical extension of the best configuration (only one component changed) and directly tests the one remaining design-space question near the optimum. As the final experiment, it maximizes the probability of either discovering a new best or confirming the current best is robust.
